x: Jim McGrath, our new member from Northern Ireland who seems to be another Mal Ash, jumped a most creditable 21'0" to finish 5th. The junior sprints illustrated our sad lack of young sprinters but this was offset to some extent by the promising debut of Linley in the 440 yds.
Jim McGrath showed his versatility by adding the discus to his list of events, and continued his battle of the "half-inch" with Dave Ansell in the long jump.
In the high hurdles Jim McGrath showed his prowess by qualifying for the final. Charlie did likewise in the 400m. hurdles and was a creditable fourth in 57·9s.
Jim McGrath, who had only just overcome an injury, was fourth in the pole vault with 11'6" - a fine effort. As he records this height every competition he should improve greatly.

The ever present Jim McGrath was second to Norman in the high-jump, and also the shot, and it was most pleaseing to see Andorka competing once more after examinations, to win the shot with a putt of 43'1½".
Jim McGrath did his usual quota of events, missing out the long-jump this time, with second place in the discus, third in the high-jump and fifth in the shot.
He, Jim McGrath,and in the late season Reg Chamberlain (just back from the Forces) represented us in most of the Long Jumps. Jim McGrath is another "Iron Man" of the calibre of Mal Ash.
An inch meant the difference between 1st and 2nd place in the Long Jump, where Dave Ansell (21'10") and Jim McGrath were squeezed out of their winner's medals.
Meanwhile, Jim McGrath was doing his usual stirling work in the field finishing fifth in the pole vault with 11'-6" and sixth in the long jump with 22'-2¼"---only 5¼" short of third place!
Dave Mitchell was another to have an off day recording a mediocre 2:1.7. Jim McGrath reached the long jump final and with a leap of 22'3¾" finished sixth.

Jim McGrath, that stalwart athlete who is the backbone of our field events section, was in fine "decathlon" form, winning the long jump, high jump and discus, and finishing third in the javelin: a fine afternoon's effort.

Jim McGrath's 11'6" gave him second place in the Pole Vault, but his jumping was affected by a badly ricked ankle. Despite this, he still took part in his usual "double", and finished 6th in the long jump with 20'11".
However, that oft - repeated maxim "success breeds success" could easily be set in motion should we discover another Mal Ash or a Jim McGrath.
In the recent Australian Veterans' Championships the pole vault was won by JIM McGRATH, once our leading field events' exponent. Nice to know that he is still keeping in trim.
"Jim McGrath is the name," he said. "You probably won't know me but I used to belong to Belgrave before emigrating in 1961."
